name: Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan Public Schools
seoTitle: District 196 Calendar: Key Dates & Official PDFs
seoDescription: Find District 196 school calendar dates, grade-specific conference days, breaks, Eastview quarter schedules, and official calendar PDFs.
districtFact: Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan Public Schools, better known as District 196, serves approximately 29,000 students across 110 square miles in the southern Twin Cities suburbs. Its calendar has one districtwide opening and grade-specific no-school dates, plus a trimester schedule for most students and a separate four-quarter track at Eastview High School.

about.title: District 196 Is the Everyday Name
about.content: The official name is Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan Public Schools, Independent School District 196. Families, the website, and the printable calendar usually lead with District 196, so both identities refer to the same south-metro system.

about.title: One Opening Date, Then a Four-Day Labor Day Pause
about.content: Unlike nearby districts that stagger opening by grade, District 196 starts all students together before Labor Day. The next Friday and Monday are no-school days, creating an unusual first week with only four student days before the long weekend.

about.title: Conference Days Affect Different Grade Levels
about.content: The printable calendar separates K-12, K-8, and 9-12 no-school dates. High school students are out for October conferences while K-8 attends; elementary and middle students are out for November and February conferences while grades 9-12 attend. The following Friday is often a districtwide high-school staff planning and learning day.

about.title: Eastview High School Uses a Different Grading Clock
about.content: Most District 196 schools follow three trimesters. Eastview High School, identified as EVHS on the PDF, follows four quarters with different boundary dates. An EVHS family should use the quarter table rather than translating district trimester endings into report-period dates.

about.title: A District Built Around Academics, Arts, and Athletics
about.content: District 196 describes its identity through a Triple-A philosophy of academics, arts, and athletics. Its network includes 20 elementary schools, six middle schools, four traditional high schools, magnet programs, the School of Environmental Studies at the Minnesota Zoo, Dakota Ridge, an Area Learning Center, and Transition Plus.

about.title: The Calendar Belongs to Mni Sota Makoce
about.content: The district acknowledges that its 110-square-mile service area is within Mni Sota Makoce, the homeland of the Dakota People, and also home to Anishinaabe and other Indigenous peoples. This local context is part of District 196's own account of the communities it serves.

calendarNotes: District 196 begins all students on one August date, then closes school the Friday before and Monday of Labor Day weekend. No-school dates must be read by the printed K-12, K-8, or 9-12 scope. High-school conference dates do not close K-8, and elementary/middle conference dates do not close grades 9-12. Most students use three trimesters, while Eastview High School uses a separate four-quarter schedule. The PDF includes staff data-analysis, planning, grading, conference, holiday, and break closures rather than labeling every student-free weekday as a holiday. The official calendar page says 2026-27 contains three additional student days because required READ Act training was completed ahead of schedule. Spanish and Somali printable versions are available for 2026-27, but the English approved calendar remains the date authority when translations disagree. School-level conferences, open houses, arts, athletics, and other events remain on each school's own calendar.

planningTips.title: Planning with the District 196 Calendar
content: Use the single August first day for all students; District 196 does not print a separate kindergarten or transition-grade opening on these approved calendars.
Plan for the Friday and Monday Labor Day closures immediately after opening week, rather than assuming the first week runs continuously into September.
Check the grade scope before arranging care: October high-school conferences are 9-12 only, while the Thursday elementary/middle conference dates are K-8 only.
Keep the following Friday separate from the K-8 conference Thursday. That Friday is usually a K-12 no-school day for high-school staff planning and learning.
Use trimester dates for most District 196 students, but use the four-quarter table for Eastview High School.
Treat post-year teacher grading and Juneteenth dates as staff or district operations after the last student day, not extensions of the student year.
Check District196.org after severe weather because both approved PDFs say the calendar is subject to change and direct families to the district for schedule updates.

livingHere.intro: District 196 follows a south-metro service area rather than one municipal boundary, covering all or part of eight cities and Vermillion Township.

highlights.label: Rosemount, Apple Valley, and Eagan
highlights.detail: The three communities in the district's formal name and the core of its public identity.

highlights.label: 110 square miles
highlights.detail: The boundary also reaches parts of Burnsville, Coates, Empire, Inver Grove Heights, Lakeville, and Vermillion Township.

highlights.label: Approximately 29,000 students
highlights.detail: District 196 identifies itself as Minnesota's third-largest school district.

highlights.label: 167,000 residents
highlights.detail: The official profile describes a multi-community population considerably larger than student enrollment.

highlights.label: School of Environmental Studies
highlights.detail: A grades 11-12 program located at the Minnesota Zoo and part of the district's broader high-school network.

highlights.label: Magnet pathways
highlights.detail: Four elementary schools and one middle school are identified as magnets within the district network.

districtFaqs.q: Is District 196 the same as Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan Public Schools?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan Public Schools is Independent School District 196, commonly shortened to District 196.

districtFaqs.q: Do all District 196 students start on the same day?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. Both reviewed approved calendars print one first day for all students, with no separate kindergarten or grade-transition opening.

districtFaqs.q: Do K-8 students have high-school conference days off?
districtFaqs.a: No. The October high-school conference day applies to grades 9-12 only. K-8 students remain in school.

districtFaqs.q: Do high-school students have elementary and middle conference days off?
districtFaqs.a: No. The Thursday conference dates in November and February apply to K-8 only. Grades 9-12 attend that day, then all K-12 students are out the following Friday.

districtFaqs.q: Does District 196 use trimesters or quarters?
districtFaqs.a: Most of the district uses three trimesters. Eastview High School uses four quarters, and its dates are printed separately on each approved calendar.

districtFaqs.q: Why does the 2026-27 calendar have three additional school days?
districtFaqs.a: The official calendar page says District 196 completed required READ Act training ahead of schedule, allowing students to have three additional school days.

districtFaqs.q: Are District 196 school events all on the one-page PDF?
districtFaqs.a: No. The PDF covers districtwide attendance dates and grading periods. Each school maintains separate calendars for conferences, open houses, activities, arts, athletics, and other local events.

customSections.label: Three No-School Labels, Three Different Plans
customSections.content: The PDF legend is operational, not decorative. The same phrase no school can apply to every student or only one grade band.

rows: Breaks, holidays, staff data analysis, planning, grading, and districtwide no-school dates

customSections.label: The EVHS Exception to the Trimester Calendar
customSections.content: The district prints trimesters as the general K-12 schedule, then explicitly routes Eastview High School to four quarters. This exception affects grading-period boundaries, not districtwide breaks or closure dates.

rows: Eastview High School students and families

customSections.label: District and School Calendars Serve Different Jobs
customSections.content: The academic PDF is the attendance baseline. The live district calendar adds Board and district events, while each school website supplies local conferences, open houses, activities, and fine-arts dates.
